title: I Gave Claude a Body
excerpt:
Try Claude free: http://clau.de/codingwithlewis

I gave Claude AI a body — a Raspberry Pi, a camera, and an RC car — then sent it into the frozen wilderness to explore completely on its own. No remote control. No pre-programmed paths. Just an AI making real-time decisions about where to go and what to look at.

What started as a hardware project I had no business attempting turned into something I didn't expect. After weeks of soldering, debugging ESC controllers, and building a custom command center from my desk, I watched this little crab-topped car find genuine wonder in frozen leaves and snowy trails.

#Pyramids #GreatPyramid #Giza #AncientEgypt #Egyptology #Archaeology #Architecture #Engineering #ConstructionHistory #RampTheory #InternalRamp #MuonTomography #GrandGallery #Megastructures #AncientEngineering
Synopsis

Two years ago, I got an email: ten years of 3D models, diagrams, and calculations—and one line that rewired everything: “the pyramids weren’t built… they were unbuilt.” This video tests that “cannibal construction” idea against the big contenders: external ramp theory, spiral ramp sightlines, and Jean-Pierre Houdin’s internal ramp with the Grand Gallery counterweight. We explain muon tomography (a CT-scan of density) and the void above the Grand Gallery, then confront the Apex Problem—how 51.84° geometry, edge visibility, and workable 7–8% inclines make finishing the top so hard. Finally, we zoom out to the Giza Plateau as a closed-loop system: overbuild → carve down → reclaim stone, plus masonry clues like bonding/keying stones—and why “missing evidence” might be design, not decay.
